name: satellite
description: The Satellite wireless-gamepad server: receives Dish clients over the LAN and plugs matching virtual controllers into the host PC

paragraphs: Low-latency Xbox controller forwarding over the network. Captures physical controller input on one machine and injects it as a virtual Xbox 360 controller on another. It handles input the way Moonlight and Sunshine do, but as a standalone tool.
Runs as a system tray application with a built-in web UI for configuration. No console window required.

TCP's reliability guarantees cause head-of-line blocking: if one packet is lost, all subsequent packets are held until retransmission completes. For controller input, only the latest state matters, so a lost packet is better than a delayed one. Moonlight, Parsec, and Steam Remote Play take the same approach.
features: System tray icon: right-click for Check for Updates, Open Web UI, Exit
Live status: packet count, sender IP, listening state
Configurable UDP port, changed via the web UI

whatItDoes.text: Low-latency Xbox controller forwarding over the network. Captures physical controller input on one machine and injects it as a virtual Xbox 360 controller on another. It handles input the way Moonlight and Sunshine do, but as a standalone tool.

requirements.text: Config lives at /Library/Application Support/satellite/config.json; the DPAPI-equivalent keyfile lives at /.config/satellite/keyfile (mode 0600). "Run at login" is a LaunchAgents plist.

Flatpak and Snap manifests also live in packaging/, but they are sideload/self-host only — neither Flathub nor the Snap Store is a viable route for an app that needs /dev/uinput, and neither format can install the udev rule that grants it.
